JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 03-11-2021 at about 6.20 p.m., the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-HW-0654 carefully and cautiously, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, near Sudhakar House, Bijjawara to Venkatagirikote road, Bijjawara village, Vijayapura Hobli.

At that time, the driver of the Maruthi Swift car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N-3746 came from Venkatagirikote to Bijjawara village with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Jain Mission Hospital, Chikkaballapura, wherein he took treatment as an in- patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was doing agriculture and vegetable business and he was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Vijayapura Police have registered the case against the driver of the Maruthi Swift car bearing No.KA-50-N-3746 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has contended that, as on the date of accident, his Maruthi Swift car bearing No.KA-50-N-3746 Raghu B.K vs Channakeshava H.M on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75856924/
2 was driven by his driver by name Manoj C., on the extreme left side of the road i.e., from Venkatagirikote towards Bijjawara village, slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations.

While so proceeding and reached near Sudhakar House, Bijjawara village, the petitioner came on his motorcycle from opposite direction i.e., from Bijjawara village towards Venkatagirikote in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations, came to his extreme right side and he himself dashed against the Swift car.

Further it is contended that, he is the R.C. owner of Maruthi Swift Car bearing No.KA-50- N-3746 and the same was insured with respondent No.2, vide policy No.0731023120P114636935, which was valid from 17-03-2021 to 16-03-2022.
The policy was valid as on the date of accident and his driver was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of accident.
He has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Whereas, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy bearing No.0731023120P114636935 in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of car bearing No.KA-50-N-3746 and its validity from 17-03-2021 to 16-03-2022.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

The petition is bad for non- joinder of necessary parties, as the owner and insurer of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-HW-0654, which was involved in the alleged accident, are proper and necessary parties.
But, they are not made as parties to the present proceedings.
It has denied the occurrence, mode of the accident and also involvement of the vehicle bearing No.KA- 50-N-3744 as alleged in the claim petition.
It has contended that, after lapse of 2 days, the petitioner has got filed a false case against he insured vehicle to cause wrongful loss to the respondent No.2.
It has contended that, the driver of the offending car was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.

It has contended that, there was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the car, the petitioner himself was riding the motorcycle in rash and negligent manner and caused the accident.

The petitioner is guilty of violation of motor vehicle rules, as he was riding the motorcycle without wearing helmet, without holding driving licence and insurance to use that vehicle on the public road and was unsafely carrying the water cans.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it has prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 03-11-2021 at about 6.30 p.m., due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Maruthi Swift Car bearing registration Raghu B.K vs Channakeshava H.M on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75856924/
3 No.KA-50-N-3746 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.

What order or Award ?
7.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked total 23 documents as Ex.P.1 to 23.
Further, he has got examined one more witness namely Dr. Girisha B.K., as P.W.2 and closed his side.
On the other hand, the respondents have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.
8. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material available on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 03-11-2021 at about 6.20 p.m., when he was riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-HW-0654 carefully, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, near Sudhakar House, Bijjawara to Venkatagirikote road, Bijjawara village,
Vijayapura Hobli, the driver of the Maruthi Swift car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N-3746 came from Venkatagirikote to Bijjawara village with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was doing agriculture and vegetable business and he was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
11. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 23 documents as Ex.
P.1 to 23

. Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report,
Ex.P.5 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.6 is true copy of charge- sheet, Ex.P.7 to 10 are discharge summaries (total 4), Ex.P.11 are medical prescriptions (total 22), Ex.P.12 are medical bills (total 225), Ex.P.13 are x-rays (total 10), Ex.P.14 is notarised copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.15 is notarised copy of driving licence, Ex.P.16 are receipts (total 5), Ex.P.17 are medical bills (total 6),
Ex.P.18 are photos (total 4), Ex.P.19 is C.D., Ex.P.20 is authorization letter, Ex.P.21 and 22 are case- sheets (total 2) and Ex.P.23 are x-rays (total 10).

4 12.

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 8, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Maruthi Swift car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N-3746 and dashing the same to an on coming motorcycle of the petitioner.
Further it reveals that, due to said impact the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his right leg.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his Ex.P.6 final report/charge-sheet that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Maruthi Swift car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N-3746.
13.

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of said car bearing Reg.
No.KA-50-N-3746 and its validity as on the date of accident
are not in dispute.

The respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied that, the above stated facts and circumstances of the accident and have taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place due to sole rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner, who came to his extreme right side and he himself dashed against the car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N- 3746 and there was no fault on the part of the driver of said car.
But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have failed to establish the said contentions.

They have neither adduced any evidence to establish the above contentions, nor they have produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Even, the respondent No.1 & 2 have not stepped into witness box to depose the contentions taken in their written statement on oath.
On the other hand, the oral evidence of P.W.1 is fully corroborated by the documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Maruthi Swift car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N-3746.

Though the learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 have cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or establishes that, accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself.

Further, the petitioner/P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestion made in his cross- examination that, the alleged accident has occurred due to his self rash and negligent driving and there was no fault on the part of driver of the car bearing Reg.
No.KA-50-N-3746.
14.

Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazer also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of the 15 feet wide Bijjawara-Venkatagirikote road, near Sudhakar's house, Bijjawara village, Vijayapura Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, due to dashing of offending car bearing Reg. No. KA-50-N-3746 to an on coming motorcycle of the petitioner.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.4, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N-3746 and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the given facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N-3746.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing has been brought out in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to negligence of the petitioner or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

The investigation officer has clearly Raghu B.K vs Channakeshava H.M on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75856924/
5 stated in his final report that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Maruthi Swift car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N-3746.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the owner or the driver of said vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
There is absolutely no material on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Maruthi Swift car bearing Reg. No.KA- 50-N-3746.
15.

Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 to 10 discharge summaries (total 4), Ex.P.13 x-rays (total 10), Ex.P.21 and 22 case-sheets (total 2) and Ex.P.23 x-rays (total 10), it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered crush injury to right fore foot, multiple and comminuted fracture of right foot metatarsals, right both bone leg fracture middle-distal junction (Type -1 compound wound), right hand 5th meta carpal neck fracture, right hand ring finger proximal phalanx fracture and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.

The same is deposed by P.W.2,
who is the doctor, who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.

On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents No.1 and 2,
to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely be held that, the respondents No.1 and 2 have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Maruthi Swift car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N-3746.
16.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

6 18.

Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the reasons stated above, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that,
he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 03-11-2021 at about 6.20 p.m., on Bijjawara-Venkatagirikote road, near Sudhakar's house, Bijjawara Village, Vijayapura Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Maruthi Swift car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N-3746.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Maruthi Swift car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N-3746 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, he has sustained crush injury to right fore foot, multiple and comminuted fracture of right foot metatarsals,
right both bone leg fracture middle-distal junction (Type -1 compound wound), right hand 5th meta carpal neck fracture, right hand ring finger proximal phalanx fracture and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e.
pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card and driving licence, which are marked as Ex.P.14 and 15.
As per Ex.P.14 and 15, the date of birth of the petitioner is 02-03-1970.
The accident has taken place on 03-11-2021 at about 6:20 p.m. Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 52 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered crush injury to right fore foot, multiple and comminuted fracture of right foot metatarsals, right both bone leg fracture middle-distal junction (Type -1 compound wound), right hand 5 th meta carpal neck fracture, right hand ring finger proximal phalanx fracture.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 38% physical disability of right lower limb and 19% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.5 wound certificate,
Ex.P.7 to 10 discharge summaries (total 4), Ex.P.13 x-rays (total 10), Ex.P.21 and 22 case-sheets (total 2) and Ex.P.23 x- rays (total 10) clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained the above injuries and he has undergone surgery for the same.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates Raghu B.K vs Channakeshava H.M on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75856924/
7 doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 03-11-2021 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 03-10-2024,
which is after lapse of two years and eleven months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.text: Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the fractures are united, the hip and knee joint are normal.

Further, he has deposed that, there is a loss of i.e., dorsiflextion 10 degree and planterflextion 20 degree in the movement of ankle, there is a half inch shortening of right limb and right foot great toe and 2nd toe got amputated at midtarsal region.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was doing agriculture and vegetable business and was earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.

Further, he has deposed that,
due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was doing agriculture and vegetable business and was earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2021.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,80,000/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 52 years is 11.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,80,000 X 12/100 X 11 = Rs.2,37,600/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.15,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 231 medical bills, as per Ex.P.12 and 17.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that, the bills at serial No.125 in Ex.P.12 and bill at serial No.1 in Ex.P.17 are one and the same.
Therefore, the bill at serial No.1 in Ex.P.17 is not taken into consideration.
Accordingly, it is held that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.5,88,106/- towards medical expenses and she is entitled for the said amount under the head of medical expenses.

8 iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. crush injury to right fore foot, multiple and comminuted fracture of right foot metatarsals, right BB leg fracture middle-distal junction (Type -1 compound wound), right hand 5th meta carpal neck fracture, right hand ring finger proximal phalanx fracture.

As per Ex.P.7 to 10 discharge summaries (total 4), the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 22 days from 03-11-2021 to 13-11-2021,
18-11-2021 to 23-11-2021, 13-01- 2022 to 13-01-2022 and 22-03-2022 to 25-03-2022, in Jain Mission Hospital, Chikkaballapura and Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru.
Further, as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.

In such circumstances,
certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.60,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

iv) Attendant charges: As per Ex.P.7 to 10 discharge summaries (total 4), the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 22 days from 03-11-2021 to 13- 11-2021, 18-11-2021 to 23-11-2021,
13-01-2022 to 13-01- 2022 and 22-03-2022 to 25-03-2022, in Jain Mission Hospital,
Chikkaballapura and Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 22 = Rs.22,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.7 to 10 discharge summaries (total 4), the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 22 days in Jain Mission Hospital, Chikkaballapura and Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 22 = Rs.17,600/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Bijjawara Village and post, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, the accident has taken place on Bijjawara-Venkatagirikote road,
near Sudhakar's house, Bijjawara Village, Vijayapura Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District and the petitioner has taken treatment at Jain Mission Hospital, Chikkaballapura and Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.6,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:

The petitioner has taken treatment for 22 days as inpatient at Jain Mission Hospital, Chikkaballapura and Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital,
Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 3 months and lost his income for the said period.
Therefore, Rs.15,000 x 3 = Rs.45,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 52 years and unfortunately he has suffered crush injury to right fore foot, multiple and comminuted fracture of right foot metatarsals, right both bone leg fracture middle-distal junction (Type -1 compound wound), right hand 5th meta carpal neck fracture, right hand ring finger proximal phalanx fracture.

The evidence shows that, he has suffered Raghu B.K vs Channakeshava H.M on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75856924/
9
permanent disability to the extent of 12% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants in the right hand.
But, admittedly the P.W.2 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery or for further treatment.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

20. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income 2,37,600-00 2.
Medical expenses 5,88,106-00 3.
Pain and sufferings 60,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 22,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 17,600-00
6. Conveyance expenses 6,000-00 7. Loss of income during 45,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 30,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses 20,000-00 Total Rs.10,26,306-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,26,306/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
21. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Maruthi Swift car bearing Reg. No. KA-50-N-3746 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

Further, as on the date of accident the driver of offending car was having valid and effective driving licence to drive the said car and the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1 was in force.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
The Vijayapura Police have registered the case against the driver of the Maruthi Swift car bearing No.KA-50-N-3746 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.arguments: It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N-3746 and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the given facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N-3746.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing has been brought out in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to negligence of the petitioner or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Maruthi Swift car bearing Reg. No.KA- 50-N-3746.
15.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely be held that, the respondents No.1 and 2 have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Maruthi Swift car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N-3746.
16.
Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was doing agriculture and vegetable business and was earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
The accident took place in 2021.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,80,000/-.
b)
Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,80,000 X 12/100 X 11 = Rs.2,37,600/-.
Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.60,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
Further, as on the date of accident the driver of offending car was having valid and effective driving licence to drive the said car and the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1 was in force.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
